questions.question: Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**revenue deficit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue deficit** arises when a **government's revenue expenditure** surpasses its revenue receipts.
 
• Revenue expenditure encompasses spending on items like salaries, pensions, and interest payments, while revenue receipts comprise income from taxes and fees.
 
• This deficit serves as a crucial gauge of the government's fiscal condition, with elevated deficits potentially triggering issues like inflation and economic instability.
 
• Various strategies exist to alleviate revenue deficits, including augmenting revenue receipts through tax hikes or fee adjustments, as well as curbing expenditure by implementing cost-saving measures or terminating certain programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• **A budget deficit** occurs when a government's total expenditures surpass its total revenues over a specified period, usually a fiscal year.
 
• This signifies that the government is spending more funds than it is generating through diverse channels like taxes, fees, and other revenue sources.
 
• Revenue receipts denote the income a business garners from its routine operations.
 
• They are recurrent and have an impact on the business's profit and loss as reflected in the income statement.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the direct outcomes that can be attributed to a good industrial sector?

options.text: Provision of mass consumption manufactured goods

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doubling of farmers’ income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Doubling of farmers' income,"** is not directly related to the** industrial sector**. 
 
• Increasing farmers' income typically involves agricultural policies, improvements in farming techniques, infrastructure development in rural areas, and market reforms to ensure fair prices for agricultural products. 
 
• While industrialization may indirectly contribute to overall economic growth and development, specifically doubling farmers' income is not a direct outcome attributed to the industrial sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• The industrial sector primarily focuses on manufacturing goods and providing employment opportunities in factories and production facilities.
 
• The outcomes typically associated with a strong industrial sector include:
 
 
• **Provision of relatively stable employment: **A robust industrial sector often leads to the creation of jobs in manufacturing industries, providing stable employment opportunities for workers.
 
• **Promotion of modernization: **Industrialization drives technological advancements and promotes modernization by encouraging the adoption of new production techniques, machinery, and processes.
 
• **Provision of mass consumption manufactured goods:** A well-developed industrial sector produces a wide range of manufactured goods, including consumer products, which are essential for meeting the demands of the population and driving economic growth through increased consumption.

questions.question: Which of the following states topped the medals tally in the Northeast Olympic Games 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manipur** secured the top spot in the **Northeast Olympic Games** for the **second consecutive time**, clinching a **total of 237 medals**, with an impressive tally of 85 golds. 
 
• **Assam **closely followed in second place, accumulating 201 medals, including 81 golds. 
 
• The event, featuring athletes from eight states in the northeast region, took place on November 10. 
 
• This victory marks Manipur's continued dominance in the Games, building upon their previous success when they hosted the inaugural edition in October 2018 and topped the medal tally with 80 golds. 
 
• Renowned for producing Olympic medalists like boxer MC Mary Kom and weightlifter Mirabai Chanu, Manipur further solidified its position by securing an additional 17 medals, including seven golds, on the final day of competition.

• Meanwhile, as preparations for the** "Manipur Olympic Games 2022" **were underway, Manipur's Chief Minister Nongthombam Biren Singh unveiled the official mascot of the event, named Nongin after the state bird of Manipur, Mrs. Hume's pheasant.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most widespread forest type in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical Deciduous Forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical deciduous forests,** also referred to as **monsoon forests,** thrive in regions receiving an annual rainfall ranging from 70 to 200 cm.
 
• These forests exhibit lush greenery and dense vegetation during the wet summer months but transform during the dry winters, characterized by leaf shedding and a drier landscape.
 
• Found in regions such as India, northern Australia, and central America, tropical deciduous forests are particularly widespread in India, covering vast areas including Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Orissa, and parts of Maharashtra.
 
• In India, these forests hold significant economic importance as they serve as abundant sources of valuable timber species like teak, sal, sandalwood, and rosewood.
 
• These trees are extensively utilized in the lumber industry for various purposes such as construction, railway infrastructure, and furniture manufacturing. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Littoral and swamp forests, commonly referred to as wetland forests, thrive in coastal regions, along seashores, creeks, river estuaries, and deltas. They can also be observed at the edges of swampy islands and along sandy beaches.
 
• **Tropical thorn forests, **characterized by scrub-like vegetation, are typically found in desert regions. These forests are prevalent in tropical and subtropical areas and thrive in semi-arid regions receiving less than 70 cm of annual rainfall.
 
• **Montane ecosystems** are situated on mountain slopes, where the alpine climate significantly influences the ecosystem. As elevation increases, temperatures drop, leading to distinct stratification within the ecosystem due to varying environmental conditions.

questions.question: What is the number of players in a Kho Kho team?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A Kho Kho team **comprises **12 players**, with **nine players** participating in a game while the remaining three serve as substitutes.
 
• During a game, the chasing team sends nine players onto the field who assume a kneeling position. Meanwhile, the defending team, comprised of the remaining three players, aims to evade being touched by members of the opposing team.
 
• Each match consists of two innings, with each team allotted seven minutes for both chasing and defending.
 
• This format allows for strategic gameplay as teams alternate between chasing and defending roles to score points and outmanoeuvre their opponents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• In** August 2022,** India introduced the inaugural league of Ultimate Kho Kho, marking the first of its kind. 
 
• Derived from the Marathi language, the name "kho kho" (खोखो) is an onomatopoeia representing the sound generated during gameplay. 
 
• The field dimensions measure 27 by 16 meters (89 by 52 feet), with a 24-meter (79-foot) separation between the two poles. 
 
• Additionally, the central lane boasts a width of 30 centimetres (12 inches), providing the setting for intense and dynamic matches within this traditional Indian sport.

questions.question: Which of the following is a plantation crop found abundantly in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tea** is a plantation crop found abundantly in** Assam**.
 
• Tea cultivation is a prominent industry in Assam, one of India's northeastern states.
 
• The region's favourable climate, with abundant rainfall and rich, loamy soil, provides optimal conditions for tea cultivation.
 
• Additionally, the low elevation and high humidity levels further contribute to the ideal environment for tea plantations. Assam's tea plantations are typically situated in the Brahmaputra River valley, where the lush greenery of the landscape is dotted with tea estates. These estates cultivate varieties of the Camellia sinensis plant, from which black tea, Assam's most renowned tea variety, is produced.
 
• The tea industry plays a significant role in Assam's economy, employing a large number of people, both directly and indirectly.
 
• Additionally, Assam's tea estates attract tourists interested in exploring the scenic beauty and heritage of tea cultivation in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uttar Pradesh** holds the distinction of being the largest producer of wheat in India.
 
• In the year 2021, the state produced an impressive quantity of over 35 million metric tons of wheat. West Bengal stands out as the leading rice-producing state in India, annually yielding approximately 146.05 lakh tons of rice.
 
• As of July 2023, Karnataka has emerged as the top maize-producing state in India, making a significant contribution of 16.45% to the nation's total maize yield.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are FALSE?

A) The impact of externality is always positive.

B) Real national income means national income at constant prices
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **externality** refers to the occurrence of a cost or benefit resulting from the actions of one party, yet borne or enjoyed financially by another.
 
• These effects may impact individuals or entire organizations and can be classified as either private or societal.
 
• **Positive externalities** arise when they provide a benefit to a third party. For instance, the construction of infrastructure like flyovers or highways can decrease transportation expenses and travel duration for users.
 
• Conversely, negative externalities occur when they impose a cost on third parties. For example, the construction of roads may lead to erosion and chemical runoff, subsequently polluting water sources downstream. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real national income, **also referred to as national income at constant prices, denotes the total income of a country adjusted for inflation.
 
• This measure, also known as nominal or money national income, reflects the actual purchasing power of a currency at a particular juncture.
 
• Constant prices, representing real value, are adjusted for price fluctuations concerning a baseline or reference point.
 
• In contrast, current prices, denoting nominal value, are those prevailing at a specific moment.
 
• Real national income offers a more precise evaluation of the real shifts in production and economic activity over time, enhancing the accuracy of comparisons.

questions.question: Which of the following grains contain oryzenin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oryzenin**, a storage protein present in rice grains, constitutes the** primary glutelin** found in **rice**, comprising approximately 75–90% of the **total protein content in rice grains.**
 
• **Extracting oryzenin** from rice grains and rice flour involves the process of sonification.
 
• Renowned for its high quality, oryzenin boasts a complete amino acid profile.
 
• Widely utilized across various food and beverage sectors, including sports nutrition, meat substitutes, bakery, and confectionery, oryzenin serves as a versatile ingredient.
 
• It emerges as an appealing option for individuals seeking lactose-free and non-allergenic protein sources.
 
• Moreover, it is favoured by those susceptible to gluten sensitivity, as it does not induce digestive complications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Rice**, a cereal grain, serves as the primary dietary staple for more than half of the global population, especially prevalent in Asia and Africa.
 
• It originates from the seeds of two grass species: Oryza sativa (Asian rice) and, less frequently, O. glaberrima (African rice).
 
• Asian rice was cultivated in China approximately 13,500 to 8,200 years ago, while African rice saw domestication in Africa around 3,000 years ago. Rice has gained widespread acceptance across diverse cultures worldwide.
 
• In 2021, global rice production reached 787 million tons, ranking it fourth among agricultural crops, following sugarcane, maize, and wheat.

questions.question:
With reference to Sonepur Cattle Fair, consider the following statements and select the correct option.

a) It is associated with the Hariharanatha temple.

b) It begins on Purnima (full moon night) and Kartik month.

c) It is celebrated in the Madhya Pradesh state.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both a and b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Sonepur Cattle Fair,** also known as Harihar Kshetra Mela, takes place on **Kartik Poornima (the full moon day)** spanning the months of **November and December in Sonepur, Bihar,** situated at the confluence of the Ganges and Gandak rivers. 
 
• Originally, the fair was held in Hajipur, with only the puja performed at the Harihar Nath temple in Sonpur. 
 
• However, during the reign of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, the fair's location shifted to Sonpur. 
 
• Legend suggests that the Harihar Nath temple was initially constructed by Lord Rama during his journey to King Janak's court to seek Mata Sita's hand. 
 
• Subsequently, Raja Man Singh undertook repairs to the temple, while its current form owes to the efforts of Raja Ram Narain, a prominent figure during the late Mughal era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Currently, the Sonepur Cattle Fair stands as one of the largest such fairs in Asia, extending from fifteen days to a month in duration.
 
• Its roots trace back to ancient times when Chandragupta Maurya (340-297 BCE) engaged in the procurement of elephants and horses across the Ganges River. Over time, it has evolved into a blend of traditional and contemporary activities.
 
• These include historical rituals like snan (ritual bathing) at various ghats and temple visits, alongside the addition of modern elements such as stalls and amusement parks.
 
• The fair encompasses a diverse array of attractions, featuring stalls representing various government departments, as well as exhibitions showcasing the talents of local artists and the merchandise of cattle traders.

questions.question: Which of the following is the proper number of electrons in 1 A of current?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.25 × 10¹⁸**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The proper number of electrons in 1 ampere (1 A) of current can be calculated using the elementary charge, which is the charge carried by a single electron.
 
• The elementary charge is approximately 1.602×10−¹⁹ coulombs.
 
• To find the number of electrons, we need to divide the total charge (which is 1 coulomb for 1 ampere of current) by the elementary charge: 

**Number of electrons= Elementary charge/Total charge ​**

Number of electrons = 1 C/1.602×10−¹⁹ C/electron

Number of electrons = 1 C/1.602×10−¹⁹ C/electron

Number of electrons ≈ 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons

So, the proper number of electrons in 1 ampere of current is approximately **6.25 × 1018 electrons**.

questions.question: In 2023, the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Government of India unveiled guidelines titled 'Endorsements Know-Hows!' that are meant for ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**social media influencers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food, and Public Distribution**, through the **Department of Consumer Affairs,** has issued a guide titled **'Endorsements Know-hows!' **targeting celebrities, influencers, and virtual influencers active on **social media platforms**.
 
• The guide's primary objective is to ensure transparency and prevent audience deception during product or service endorsements.
 
• It emphasizes adherence to the Consumer Protection Act and relevant regulations.
 
• It addresses individuals or groups with the ability to influence their audience's purchasing decisions or opinions due to their authority, expertise, position, or relationship with their followers.
 
• The guide particularly highlights situations where there exists a material connection between an advertiser and a celebrity/influencer, potentially impacting the credibility or significance of the endorsement made by the celebrity/influencer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Social media influencers **are individuals who have established credibility and expertise in a particular subject matter.
 
• Through consistent posts on their preferred social media platforms, they attract sizable followings of enthusiastic and engaged individuals who value their opinions.
 
• Brands often favour social media influencers due to their ability to initiate trends and persuade their followers to purchase the products they endorse.

questions.question: In India which of the following statements is NOT correct about Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To organise village panchayat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles of State Policy, and Fundamental Duties** are integral sections of the Constitution of India, delineating the essential obligations of the state towards its citizens, as well as the rights and duties of citizens towards the State.
 
• These sections are regarded as fundamental components of the constitution, which was crafted by the Constituent Assembly of India between 1947 and 1949.
 
• The Fundamental Duties encompass the moral obligations of all citizens to foster patriotism and uphold India's unity, as outlined in **Part IV–A of the Constitution.**
 
• These duties, akin to the Directive Principles, are not directly enforceable by courts unless enacted into law by the legislature, impacting both individuals and the nation as a whole.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• **List of Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Abide by the Constitution and respect the national flag & National Anthem
 
• Follow the ideals of the freedom struggle
 
• Protect the sovereignty & integrity of India
 
• Defend the country and render national services when called upon
 
• Spirit of common brotherhood
 
• Preserve composite culture
 
• Preserve natural environment
 
• Develop scientific temper
 
• Safeguard public property
 
• Strive for excellence
 
• Duty fo all parents/guardians to send their children in the age group of 6-14 years to school.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the rationales behind microfinance?

options.text: Many innovative institutional mechanisms have developed across the world to enhance credit to the poor even in the absence of formal mortgages.
More than access to credit poor need subsidies
The absence of formal employment makes the poor non 'bankable'.
More than subsidies poor need access to credit

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**More than access to credit poor need subsidies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Microfinance services** cater to unemployed or low-income individuals who often lack access to traditional financial institutions due to poverty or limited financial resources, enabling them to secure small business loans safely and ethically.
 
• While microfinance initiatives are global, the majority are concentrated in developing nations like **Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Afghanistan, Democratic Republic of Congo, Indonesia, and Ecuador**, where they play a crucial role in fostering economic empowerment and poverty alleviation. 
 
• The advantages of microfinance extend beyond merely providing capital to individuals; entrepreneurs who establish successful businesses through microfinance can further contribute to their communities by generating employment opportunities and facilitating trade, thereby fostering overall socio-economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• While certain **microfinance interest rates** may be lower compared to traditional banks, critics argue that some operations are profiting from the impoverished population.
 
• Moreover, the involvement of major financial institutions and large corporations in launching for-profit microfinance departments has raised concerns that higher interest rates imposed by these entities could potentially lead to a debt trap for low-income borrowers, overshadowing the intended benefits.
 
• Nevertheless, microfinance serves as a crucial form of banking service for low-income individuals or groups who lack access to conventional financial services.

questions.question: In 2006, Ileana Citaristi, an Italian Odissi dancer, was awarded with the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Shri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2006, Ileana Citaristi,** an Italian Odissi dancer, was awarded with **the ****Padma Shri**.
 
• Ileana Citaristi, an Italian dancer proficient in Odissi and Chhau, as well as a dance instructor based in Bhubaneswar, India, was honored with the 43rd National Film Award for Best Choreography for her work in the film Yugant in 1995. 
 
• Notably, in 2006, she became the first dancer of foreign origin to receive the Padma Shri award for her remarkable contributions to Odissi. 
 
• Additionally, she has been bestowed with the 'Raseshwar Award' by the Sur Singar Sansad, Mumbai. 
 
• Recognizing her significant impact on Odissi, the Government of India conferred upon her the Padma Shri in 2006. 
 
• Furthermore, in 2008, the Italian government bestowed upon her the title of a member of the Order of the Star of Italian Solidarity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Padma Bhushan** is a distinguished civilian award bestowed by the Government of India to individuals for their exceptional service and contributions in various fields.
 
• **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award, is conferred upon individuals for their outstanding achievements and contributions to the nation's progress and welfare.
 
• **Padma Shri, **a prestigious civilian honour, is awarded by the Government of India to individuals in recognition of their distinguished service and significant accomplishments in various spheres.
 
• **Padma Vibhushan,** one of India's highest civilian honours, is bestowed upon individuals for their exceptional contributions and achievements in diverse fields, recognizing their outstanding impact on the nation's development and welfare.

questions.question: Which essential amino acid is necessary for the production of our brain's chemical messengers including melatonin, dopamine, noradrenaline and thyroxine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phenylalanine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phenylalanine** is a type of amino acid, which exists in three forms: L-, D-, and DL-phenylalanine. L-phenylalanine is naturally occurring and can be found in foods like meat and eggs.
 
• Amino acids serve as the fundamental building blocks of proteins, with L-phenylalanine being classified as an essential amino acid. It is the sole form of phenylalanine present in proteins.
 
• Conversely, D-phenylalanine is not considered an essential amino acid, and its physiological role remains unclear.
 
• DL-phenylalanine is synthesized in laboratory settings. Phenylalanine is utilized by individuals for various purposes, including the treatment of vitiligo (a condition characterized by white patches on the skin), attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), chronic pain, signs of aging skin, depression, and numerous other conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Leucine** is among the three essential branched-chain amino acids. These amino acids play a crucial role in providing energy to skeletal muscle during exercise.
 
• **Tryptophan **is an essential amino acid vital for normal growth in infants and for the synthesis and maintenance of the body's proteins, muscles, enzymes, and neurotransmitters.
 
• **Valine**, another essential branched-chain amino acid, is utilized by the body to aid in energy production.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the category of Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nehruvian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nehruvian** is NOT included in the** category of Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• **The Directive Principles of State Policy **in India are categorized into several groups: **Economic and Socialistic, Political and Administrative, Justice and Legal, Environmental, Protection of Monuments, Peace and Security. **
 
• These principles serve as guidelines for the governance of the country by the government of India. 
 
• While not enforceable by any court, they are deemed fundamental in the administration of the nation, making it the responsibility of the State to incorporate these principles into the formulation of laws to establish a fair society. 
 
• These principles draw inspiration from similar directives outlined in the Constitution of Ireland, which pertain to social justice, economic welfare, foreign policy, and legal and administrative affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In 1928, the **Nehru Commission, **which included representatives from all Indian political parties, put forward constitutional reforms for India.
 
• These reforms advocated for dominion status for India, elections conducted through universal suffrage, and the assurance of fundamental rights.
 
• Additionally, the proposals aimed to provide representation for religious and ethnic minorities while also restraining the powers of the government.
 
• In 1931, the Indian National Congress, the predominant political party at the time, adopted resolutions affirming its commitment to safeguarding fundamental civil rights.
 
• Furthermore, the Congress pledged to promote socio-economic rights such as establishing a minimum wage and abolishing untouchability and serfdom. These resolutions demonstrated the Congress's dedication to the principles of socialism.

questions.question: The music legend Jagjit Singh is associated with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghazal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jagjit Singh** was a renowned Indian composer, singer, and musician recognized for his contributions across multiple languages.
 
• He is widely credited with revitalizing and **popularizing ghazal,** a traditional Indian art form, by selecting poetry that resonated with the masses and composing it in a manner that emphasized the significance of words and the melodies they invoked.
 
• His approach to composing and singing, characterized by a focus on lyrical content, is regarded as Bol-pradhan in the realm of Indian classical music.
 
• In recognition of his outstanding achievements, Jagjit Singh was honoured with the Padma Bhushan, one of India's highest civilian awards, bestowed upon him by the government in 2003.
 
• Additionally, in February 2014, the government released a commemorative set of two postal stamps as a tribute to his enduring legacy and contributions to music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The ghazal,** originating from Arabic poetry, is a form of amatory poem or ode. These poetic compositions typically explore themes of spiritual and romantic love, offering a nuanced reflection on the complexities of human emotions. 
 
• **Classical music** typically denotes the sophisticated and complex art music of the Western world, which is traditionally distinguished from Western folk music or popular music traditions. 
 
• **Western music, **also known as Western or cowboy music, is a genre of music that originated in the Western United States and Western Canada, reflecting the experiences, lifestyles, and landscapes of the people who settled and worked in these regions.

questions.question: What is the classical dance of Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya Nritya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sattriya Nritya** is the classical dance of **Assam**.
 
• Sattriya Nritya holds a significant position among Indian classical dances. Initially conceived as part of Bhaona, performances of Ankiya Nat, one-act plays, the art form was pioneered by Sankardev, a polymath from **Assam during the 15th-16th century**.
 
• These dances are integral to the living traditions of Sattra communities, which comprise devotees adhering to the Ekasarana Dharma, a Hindu sect established by Sankardev.
 
• The themes depicted in Sattriya Nritya revolve around Krishna, along with other avatars of Vishnu like Rama, and narratives from revered epics such as the Mahabharata and the Ramayana.
 
• In a significant recognition, the Sangeet Natak Akademi of India conferred classical status upon Sattriya on November 15, 2000, thereby acknowledging it as one of the eight classical dances of India.
 
• Modern iterations of Sattriya delve into various themes and narratives, and its performances enjoy global stages, captivating audiences worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a revered Indian classical dance form with its origins rooted in Tamil Nadu. Recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, it serves as a medium for conveying South Indian religious themes and spiritual concepts.
 
• Kathak, another esteemed ancient Indian classical dance, is believed to have evolved from the wandering bards of North India known as Kathakars, or storytellers.
 
• **Kuchipudi, **one of the eight major Indian classical dances, traces its roots to the village of Kuchipudi in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: The Pala Dynasty rulers were primarily patrons of which religion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhist**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Pala Dynasty rulers were primarily patrons **Buddhist**.
 
• The Pāla Empire emerged as a dominant force in the Indian subcontinent during the post-classical period, with its roots in the Bengal region.
 
• Named after its ruling dynasty, characterized by rulers bearing names ending with the suffix Pāla, which signifies "protector" in Prakrit, the empire's foundation can be traced back to the late eighth century CE, with the ascension of Gopāla as the emperor of Gauda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Pāla Empire** exerted its influence primarily in Bengal and eastern Bihar, encompassing key cities such as Gauḍa, Vikramapura, Pāṭaliputra, Monghyr, Somapura, Ramavati (Varendra), Tāmralipta, and Jaggadala.
 
• This period is regarded as one of the golden eras in Bengali history, marked by stability and prosperity brought forth by the Palas after centuries of internal strife and civil war among rival factions.
 
• Under Pāla rule, there was significant advancement in various aspects of Bengali civilization, with notable contributions to arts and architecture.
 
• The Palas not only built upon the achievements of preceding Bengali civilizations but also produced remarkable works of art and architectural marvels, further enriching the cultural heritage of the region.

questions.question: Those engaged in agriculture in India suffer from which of these unemployment types?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Disguised Unemployment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Disguised unemployment **refers to a situation where a portion of the labour force **either remains jobless or is employed **in a manner that contributes negligibly to productivity.
 
• Despite being technically unemployed, these workers do not impact the overall output of the economy.
 
• This phenomenon arises when productivity levels are low, and an excessive number of workers are engaged in jobs that do not require their full capacity.
 
• Disguised unemployment is commonly observed in developing countries, where the sizeable population results in a surplus of labour.
 
• It is typically associated with low productivity and often coincides with informal and agricultural labour markets, which can absorb a significant number of workers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Frictional unemployment **arises from the transition period between leaving one job voluntarily and securing another. It reflects the time gap between job changes, during which individuals actively seek new employment opportunities.
 
• **Technological unemployment** occurs when advancements in technology, such as automation and artificial intelligence (AI), lead to the displacement of human workers from their jobs.
 
• **Structural unemployment i**s a type of involuntary unemployment caused by a fundamental mismatch between the skills possessed by the workforce and the demands of the job market.

questions.question: Which Indian state was the first to make it mandatory for all homes to have rooftop rainwater harvesting structures?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu **set a pioneering precedent in India by **instituting mandatory rooftop rainwater harvesting **in 2001, a policy that remains unique to the state.
 
• Amendments were introduced to the** Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act of 1920** and the Building Rules of 1973, mandating the incorporation of rainwater harvesting structures in all new constructions.
 
• Furthermore, the Ministry of Urban Affairs and Poverty Alleviation has extended this mandate nationally, requiring rainwater harvesting for new buildings with a roof area exceeding 100 square meters and plots larger than 1,000 square meters.
 
• The implementation of Tamil Nadu's rainwater harvesting model has yielded notable results, evidenced by a 50% increase in water levels in Chennai within five years. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tamil Nadu,** situated in the southernmost part of India, stands as the tenth-largest state in terms of area and the sixth-largest in terms of population.
 
• It is predominantly inhabited by the Tamil people, who speak the Tamil language—a language of ancient lineage and official status.
 
• The capital and largest city of Tamil Nadu is Chennai.
 
• Geographically, Tamil Nadu is positioned on the southeastern coast of the Indian peninsula. It is bordered by the Western Ghats and Deccan Plateau to the west, the Eastern Ghats to the north, and the Eastern Coastal Plains along the Bay of Bengal to the east.
 
• To the southeast, it is bounded by the Gulf of Mannar and the Palk Strait, while the southernmost tip is washed by the Laccadive Sea. The river Kaveri traverses the state, dividing it into distinct regions.

questions.question: In which year did the Central Statistical Office adopt the GVA concept in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **Gross Value Added (GVA) **at basic prices originates from the** United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA),** which was introduced in 1993 and maintained in the SNA 2008 revision as part of the overhaul of compilation and classification systems.
 
• This framework was subsequently adopted by the Central Statistical Office (CSO) during its base revision in** January 2015**.
 
• **Gross Value Added (GVA) **is defined as the value of output minus the value of intermediate consumption.
 
• It represents the contribution of both labour and capital to the production process.
 
• When taxes on products (net of subsidies on products) are included, the sum of value added across all resident units yields the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a nation.
 
• Hence, the GDP of any country reflects the total Gross Value Added (GVA) across all sectors of the economy during the specified year, adjusting for taxes and subsidies, without accounting for capital consumption or depreciation. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In India, the estimation of **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** is undertaken by the** Central Statistical Office (CSO).**
 
• The Ministry of Finance utilizes the GDP figures (at current prices) to establish fiscal targets by the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act of 2003 and its associated regulations.
 
• As part of this process, the Ministry of Finance formulates its projections regarding GDP for the upcoming two years while delineating future fiscal objectives.
 
• Gross Value Added (GVA) at basic prices is delineated as the output valued at basic prices minus the intermediate consumption valued at purchasers' prices. In this context, GVA is identified by the price at which the output is appraised.

questions.question: Who among the following Indian sportswomen has received the BBC Indian Sportswoman of The Year 2022 award?

questions.question: As of 1 April 2023, how many national laboratories does the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR) have in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**37**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR),** renowned for its forefront research and development (R&D) expertise across various scientific and technological domains, stands as a modern R&D institution.
 
• CSIR boasts a vibrant network comprising **37 national laboratories, 39 outreach centers,** 1 Innovation Complex, and three units with a widespread presence throughout India.
 
• Encompassing a broad spectrum of scientific and technological fields, CSIR's areas of focus span from oceanography, geophysics, chemicals, and drugs to genomics, biotechnology, and nanotechnology, as well as extending to mining, aeronautics, instrumentation, environmental engineering, and information technology.
 
• CSIR plays a crucial role in providing significant technological advancements across numerous societal domains, including environment, health, drinking water, food, housing, energy, and both farm and non-farm sectors.
 
• Moreover, CSIR contributes significantly to the development of human resources in science and technology, underscoring its pivotal role in shaping the landscape of scientific and technological innovation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to the S**cimago Institutions Ranking World Report 2021, CSIR** is distinguished as the sole Indian institution ranked within the top 100 global government institutions, securing the 37th position out of 1,587 government organizations worldwide. 
 
• In the Asian region, CSIR holds an impressive 7th rank, solidifying its leadership within India as the top-ranked institution.
